clauses.requirement: The ESA (electrical/electronic sub-assembly, e.g. the LED rear lamp electronics) shall comply with the general test requirements for radiated immunity testing set out in UN R10 Annex 9 paragraph 3 (frequency range, dwell times, test intervals and failure verification).

For the ESA state during tests (Annex 9 para 2.3), when tested in the REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid: the REESS shall be in charging mode; its state of charge shall be kept between 20 and 80 per cent of maximum SOC during the whole measurement (measurement may be split into time slots, discharging the traction battery before the next slot); if current consumption is adjustable, it shall be set to at least 20 per cent of maximum rated charging/input current for AC charging, and for DC charging to at least 20 per cent of nominal value or a minimum of 16 A if 20 per cent cannot be achieved in the test facility, unless another value is agreed with the Type-Approval Authorities; for multiple batteries the average SOC shall be considered; failure criteria: temporary loss of charging function is allowed provided there is no incorrect charging condition (e.g. over-current, overvoltage) and the function can be restored by simple intervention without tools, such as turning the DUT off/on, after the disturbance is removed.

Any extraneous equipment required to operate the ESA under test shall not be in place during the calibration phase, and no extraneous equipment shall be closer than 1 m from the reference point during calibration.

To ensure reproducible results when tests and measurements are repeated, the test signal generating equipment and its layout shall be to the same specification as that used during each appropriate calibration phase.

If the ESA under test consists of more than one unit, the interconnecting cables should ideally be the wiring harnesses intended for use in the vehicle; if not available, the length between the electronic control unit and the AN shall be as defined in the standard; all cables in the harness should be terminated as realistically as possible, preferably with real loads and actuators.
The ESA shall meet the general test requirements of UN R10 Annex 9 paragraph 3, covering frequency range and dwell times, test intervals, and verification of failures.

Measurements shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1, with test signal modulation: (a) AM, 1 kHz, 80 per cent modulation depth in 20 to 400 MHz; (b) PM2, Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs in 2,700 to 3,100 MHz; (c) PM3, Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs in 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz; unless otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer; frequency step size and dwell time shall be chosen according to ISO 11452-1.

The Technical Service shall perform the test at the intervals specified in ISO 11452-1 throughout 20 to 6,000 MHz; alternatively, if the manufacturer provides measurement data for the whole band from a test laboratory accredited to the applicable parts of ISO 17025 and recognized by the Type Approval Authority, the Technical Service may choose a reduced number of spot frequencies (e.g. 27, 45, 65, 90, 120, 150, 190, 230, 280, 380, 450, 600, 750, 900, 1,300, 1,800, 2,360, 2,600, 3,000, 3,600, 5,200 and 5,900 MHz) to confirm the ESA meets the requirements of this Annex. If an ESA fails the tests, it shall be verified as having failed under the relevant test conditions and not as a result of the generation of uncontrolled fields.
